research_period: Milan, Paris and Pitti Uomo menswear shows, June 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Global: Milan, Paris and Florence runways; premium and mid-market menswear
title: SS27 Men's Trim Market Strategy
summary: In a low-growth 2027, use piping, embroidery and pocket details to update core menswear; keep hand-applied studs and beading for premium pieces.

sections.heading: The market context
sections.body: Fashion is expected to remain in low single-digit growth in 2027, with high freight, energy and financing costs, and markdown risk from excess stock<sup>[1]</sup>. In the EU, large companies may not destroy certain unsold apparel since 19 July 2026<sup>[1]</sup>.

sections.heading: Build, test, sell through
sections.body:
| Action | Trims |
|---|---|
| Build | Contrast piping, flat pockets, embroidered motifs |
| Test | Studs and stones<sup>[2]</sup>, bird embroidery<sup>[2]</sup>, beading |
| Sell through | Heavy distressing and logo hardware |

sections.heading: By market
sections.body:
- **India and the Gulf:** embroidery and piping suit festive and resort dressing; India's GDP grew 7.8% year on year in the second quarter of 2026<sup>[1]</sup>.
- **Europe:** keep trims modular so unsold stock can be reworked.
- **United States:** use trims to differentiate core shirts at full price.

design_implications: - Design trims that can be added late (embroidery, piping) to respond to sales.
commercial_implications: - Track sell-through by trim variant and chase winners.
